items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: Guys like Shadow Wilson and Miles Davis and Ella Fitzgerald and Hot Lips Page, and all those kind of people.

ctx.x: Yeah, he had this five string bass. But you know later on I discovered that Slam Stewart tuned his bass with a high C on top. And I didn’t realize that at the time. And then in that little corner we had the Hi-Hat, we had all the jazz cats come over there. Are you familiar with Boston? Mass Columbus? We had that little corner, we had Wally’s across the street where I met Pops Foster. Pops Foster was 75 about that time and he was claimed to be the first guy to begin plucking the bass. And I said, “Pops, come on…

and he says, “good sound.” And you know, encouragement. And in this little joint, Eddie Levine’s, I met all kinds of musicians, they used to come up and visit our leader, who was Dean Earl. And as far as my style and being a gentleman and being in the business and all that, was a fellow by the name of, like I said, his name was Dean Earl.
